ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (AML/CFT Act), as amended by the AML/CFT Amendment Acts 2017 and 2023; Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008 (FSP Act); Companies Act 1993 (ss 20–23 on names, s 187 registered office, ss 86–95 share registers and beneficial ownership record-keeping); Companies (Name Approval) Regulations 2014; United Nations Act 1946 and United Nations Sanctions Regulations; Sanctions Act 2020 and Russia Sanctions Act 2022; Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism (Name Checking) Regulations 2021; Financial Markets Authority (FMA) AML/CFT Beneficial Ownership Guidance (2020); FMA Politically Exposed Persons Guidance (2018); Reserve Bank of New Zealand Fit and Proper Policy for any stored-value or deposit-adjacent characterization; Income Tax Act 2007 and Tax Administration Act 1994 (tax residence and foreign-sourced income characterization reserved for Stage 3 tax opinion). The 'International Company' is structured for the purposes of this Stage 1 dossier as a New Zealand-incorporated private company limited by shares under the Companies Act 1993; any special 'tax-exempt zone' classification is an internal pipeline attribute to be validated at the corporate tax compliance stage.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized and apostilled Certificate of Incorporation and Memorandum/Articles of Association of each direct corporate shareholder and of each entity at or above the 25% UBO threshold
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry or equivalent corporate registry in the shareholder's country of origin (e.g., Hong Kong Companies Registry; Singapore Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the competent authority of the origin jurisdiction; New Zealand is a Hague Apostille Convention member and will recognize apostilles from other member states directly

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized passport bio-data page and proof of residential address for each ultimate beneficial owner who is a natural person controlling, directly or indirectly, 25% or more of the International Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed notary public in the UBO's country of residence, with attestation by the designated competent authority of that country (e.g., Hong Kong High Court Apostille Service)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille from the origin state; if the origin state is not a Hague member, chain consular legalization at the nearest New Zealand Embassy or Consulate is required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or Certificate of Incumbency for any corporate parent, guarantor, or programme manager executing the virtual card issuer's commercial agreements
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry or licensed corporate services provider in the parent entity's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille in the origin state and, where requested by the New Zealand AML/CFT supervisor, additional consular authentication by the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade Legalisation Unit

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Ultimate Beneficial Ownership Statutory Declaration (pre-incorporation AML/CFT declaration) disclosing legal name, nationality, tax residence, shareholding percentages, control chain, and source of funds of each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand-incorporated local agent acting as proposed AML/CFT compliance officer; declarant executes before a New Zealand Justice of the Peace or notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: New Zealand statutory declaration witnessed domestically; all foreign witness signatures on supporting evidentiary documents must be notarized and apostilled

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter in respect of each material funding source and each UBO, issued on the regulated institution's letterhead
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed bank or licensed financial institution in the UBO's country of residence; the reference must state account conduct, duration of relationship, and confirmation that the UBO passed the issuing institution's own KYC/CDD process
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized signature of the issuing officer followed by apostille of the notarization; for non-Hague origin states, consular legalization via the New Zealand diplomatic mission

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), ss 12 (Registration of company), 14 (Registrar's duty before incorporation), 15 (Certificate of incorporation), 16 (Effect of registration and full capacity), 28-36 (Constitution), 46 (Shares and consideration), 96 (Pre-emptive rights), 180 (Registered office), 150-153 (Directors), and 386-387 (Restoration/removal) — read together with the Companies (Incorporation) Regulations 2013. The 'International Company' (IC) designation is a constitutional and share-structuring overlay on a private limited liability company; it is not a distinct statutory vehicle under New Zealand law. The IC tax envelope relies on non-resident ownership, non-resident taxation of non-New Zealand sourced card-issuance revenue, and the absence of a New Zealand permanent establishment.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies), Consumer Protection and Compliance, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), Level 6, 15 Stout Street, Wellington 6011, New Zealand; online register: www.companiesoffice.govt.nz
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 2 — Application for Incorporation of a New Company submitted electronically through the New Zealand Companies Register; supported by Form 4 — Consent to Act as Director (and Shareholder consent where applicable), a formal Constitution (where adopted), registered-office premises consent, and notarized identity dossiers. The Certificate of Incorporation is issued electronically by the Registrar upon effective registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under Companies Act 1993; incorporation may proceed with zero or nominal subscribed capital, and no escrow account, capital guarantee, or trust reserve is required. For the IC envelope, one subscriber share of NZ$1 is routinely fully paid, with further funding advanced as non-resident shareholder loan accounts carried at commercial arm's length; the Companies Office confirms no minimum capital threshold for FSP registration of a virtual card issuer, although the FMA-sponsored e-money risk practice recommends maintaining at least NZ$50,000 net tangible equity for prudential credibility.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [INTERNATIONAL COMPANY NAME] LIMITED (THE 'COMPANY'), HELD AT [REGISTERED OFFICE ADDRESS, NEW ZEALAND] ON [DATE] AT 10:00 AM.

ATTENDANCE: [Director A] (Chair), [Director B], [Director C], [Company Secretary]; all directors entitled to vote were present and waived notice in writing.

1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION. RESOLVED, as a special resolution, that the subscription statement and allotment of [NUMBER] ordinary shares of NZ$0.01 each, fully paid, as set forth in the incorporation application, be and are hereby ratified, approved and confirmed; FURTHER RESOLVED that amounts contributed by non-resident shareholders beyond stated capital be credited to a Shareholders' Loan Account bearing arm's-length interest, repayable on demand and subordinated to any future regulated creditors.
2. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION. RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company shall be maintained at [ADDRESS, CITY, NEW ZEALAND] in compliance with s 180 of the Companies Act 1993; that the owner's consent to occupy and hold the premises as the registered office be filed with the Registrar; and that [AGENT NAME] be appointed agent for service of process, notices, and any court or regulatory documents in New Zealand.
3. APPOINTMENT OF OFFICERS. RESOLVED that [Director A] be and is hereby appointed Managing Director, [Director B] appointed Chief Financial Officer, and [Name] appointed Company Secretary, each to serve until removal by the Board, and each to exercise powers conferred by the Company's Constitution and the Companies Act 1993.
4. BOARD AM/LCFT AND COMPLIANCE DELEGATION. RESOLVED that the AML/CFT Compliance Programme prepared for the virtual-card issuing business be adopted; that [Officer Name] be appointed AML/CFT Compliance Officer in accordance with the AML/CFT Act 2009; and that the audit, compliance and risk committee be constituted with written terms of reference.
5. BANK AND CARD SPONSORSHIP AUTHORITY. RESOLVED that the Company open corporate bank and settlement accounts with [Sponsor Bank], authorize the BIN Sponsorship and Programme Manager Agreements with Mastercard/Visa networks, and approve joint signing authority: any two of [Officers list] (or equivalent electronic approvals) to bind the Company for transactions above NZ$10,000, with single signatures below that threshold.
6. GOVERNANCE CHARTER. RESOLVED that the Corporate Governance Charter, Board Committee Charters, insider-trading policy, and delegated authority register be hereby approved; and the Secretary is directed to circulate the same to all shareholders and officers.

There being no further business, the meeting was declared closed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Security Name Reservation and Registry Availability Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: NZ Companies Office — Company Names and Reserved Names Register (online portal operated by the Registrar of Companies, MBIE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lodge a company name reservation through the New Zealand Companies Register using the electronic name-availability tool. The proposed IC name must include the mandatory suffix 'Limited' or 'Ltd', must not contravene s 20 of the Companies Act 1993 (undesirable names), and must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name. The name search covers phonetic similarity, Maori usage, and internationally protected identifiers. Reserve the cleared name for a priority period of 20 business days, during which the incorporation application must be lodged.
required_dossiers: Online name reservation form (proposed name plus two alternatives)
Form NZ-NAME1 statutory declaration of name distinctiveness (if requested)
Legal opinion or trademark clearance memorandum (where conflict is reasonably foreseeable)
Certificate of non-availability search result printed from the Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar refuses reservation under the undesirable-name provisions, the applicant may file a notice of objection or written representation within 10 working days and receive a written Registrar's decision; simultaneously select and reserve an alternative cleared name to preserve the filing timeline and re-file the incorporation application under the revised corporate designation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Constitution, Shareholder Subscription and Registered Office Arrangements
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporating legal counsel and registered-office accommodation provider (pre-filing arrangement; no Registry action in this step)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before lodgement, draft the written Constitution of the Company under ss 28-36 of the Companies Act 1993, incorporating provisions for share classes (e.g. ordinary voting shares, dividend-bearing but non-voting shares for treasury investors, and a statutory holdback), permitted creditor priority, director powers, indemnity and insurance, arbitration of shareholder disputes, and the NZ registered-office clause. Obtain a dedicated New Zealand registered office address with evidence of the owner's written consent for use as registered office and service of process. Secure each founding director's consent to act, each shareholder's subscription statement, and a declaration confirming 100% non-resident beneficial ownership for the IC tax-envelope classification.
required_dossiers: Signed Constitution (original or electronic execution)
Consent of registered-office premises owner to the Registrar
Shareholder subscription statements quantifying subscribed shares and share premium
Form 4 Consent to Act for each proposed director
Declaration of non-resident ownership (provide personal TINs, passports, and residential addresses)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any consent or declaration is defective, re-execute and re-date the instrument, obtain replacement consent, or substitute the officer/office prior to lodgement; if the Registrar later queries the constitution, file a special resolution to alter the constitution under s 35 and notify the Registrar of the amendment without disturbing the incorporation date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Incorporation Application Lodgement and Statutory Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of New Zealand Companies — Companies Register online electronic lodgement (MBIE validation unit)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form 2 (Application for Incorporation of a New Company) on the Companies Register and attach the executed Constitution, the Form 4 consents, registered-office consent, and notarized identity and address dossiers for every director and shareholder. Declare the number of shares, par value, and total consideration, and answer the statutory disqualification questions (undischarged bankrupts, prohibited persons, and persons disqualified by the Financial Markets Authority). Pay the statutory fee of NZ$160 (inclusive of NZ-GST; ~USD 100.80) by credit card or debit instrument. On clean validation, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation electronically, typically within minutes of a business-day submission; statutory service standard is 2 working days.
required_dossiers: Form 2 — Application for Incorporation of a New Company (online)
Form 4 — Notice of Consent to Act for each director
Signed Constitution (filed copy)
Consent from registered-office owner
Notarized passport copies, proof of residential address, and original birth/passport details for directors and shareholders
Subscriber statement of share capital and par value
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a query or defect notice under s 14, correct and re-submit the deficient fields within 5 working days of receipt of the notice; where the company name is rejected, secure a fresh name reservation and re-file; if the Registrar refuses registration, apply for a written decision and seek declaratory relief in the High Court of New Zealand, while concurrently lodging a perfected second application to protect precedence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certification of Incorporation and Corporate Legal File Compilation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: NZ Companies Office (electronic certificate issuance) and the incorporating agent/registered office service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon issuance, download the electronic Certificate of Incorporation and the company extract from the Companies Register. Verify the company number, date of registration, registered office, balance date, and shareholder profile in the public register. Compile the company legal kit: minute book (or digital minute repository), share certificates, share register, directors' interest register, common seal (optional under s 93), and the constitutional instruments. File the original certificate together with the signed incorporators' application and statutory consents in the corporate records of the IC.
required_dossiers: Electronic Certificate of Incorporation
Companies Register company extract (registered office, directors, shareholders)
Minute book and board resolution register
Blank share certificates and common seal (optional)
Initial directors' and shareholders' registers under ss 83-89 and 96-100 of the Companies Act 1993
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate evidence is lost or defective, request a certified printed copy from the Registrar; if the registered office or director details are inaccurate, correct the register of directors under s 156 and file the required notice with the Registrar; for any registry error, apply for a rectification order under s 158 of the Companies Act 1993.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: New Zealand Tax Registrations — IRD Number, GST and Non-Resident Withholding Tax (NRWT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue New Zealand — Business Registration and Compliance Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the incorporated company for an IRD number with Inland Revenue within 20 working days after formation as required by s 24B(2)(e) of the Tax Administration Act 1994. Submit the IRD company registration form declaring the start date, expected New Zealand-sourced income, and 100% non-resident shareholding status. Register for GST if actual or expected New Zealand taxable supplies exceed NZ$60,000 in any 12-month period (or voluntarily at 15%) and for Non-Resident Withholding Tax (NRWT) on any interest, dividend, or deemed royalties paid to non-resident shareholders at prescribed rates under the NZ-US/China/OECD double tax agreements or the domestic NRWT schedule. For the IC tax envelope, complete an entity self-review confirming no New Zealand permanent establishment and no New Zealand-source income from remote virtual-card issuing.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and company extract
IRD Company Registration form (IR 742 or online equivalent)
Notarized passports and tax identification numbers (TINs) of directors/shareholders
Declaration of non-resident ownership and tax residency certificates (IRD request form IR873)
GST registration declaration (activity and expected turnover)
Registered office address and contact information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD disallows the non-resident tax status or imposes NRWT classification, file a notice of adjustment within the statutory response period with supportive OECD tax-residency certificates; if the GST registration is queried, provide a revised turnover projection and register from a zero date; for late registration, apply under s 24B for administrative penalty remission and enter into an instalment arrangement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Financial Service Provider (FSP) Registration and Approved Dispute Resolution Scheme Enrolment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Financial Service Providers (Companies Office, MBIE) and the Financial Markets Authority (FMA) as appeals/monitoring authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for FSP registration under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008 prior to providing financial services in or from New Zealand. On the FSP-1 online form, select the applicable financial service categories, in particular the issuance and management of means of payment (virtual expense cards), and appoint a compliance officer resident in New Zealand. Join a FMA-approved external dispute resolution (EDR) scheme (e.g. Financial Dispute Resolution Service) and obtain the scheme's certificate. The IC's registration is recorded on the public FSP Register, and the company receives an FSP number allowing legal fintech operation and sponsor-bank onboarding.
required_dossiers: FSP-1 electronic application (company details, nature and category of financial services)
Certificate of Incorporation and full corporate extract
Board resolution authorizing FSP application and names of directors and senior managers
Approved dispute resolution scheme membership certificate
AML/CFT compliance officer appointment and CV
Non-resident ownership and IC governance structure declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar suspends or queries the FSP application, furnish additional corporate governance, ownership, and AML/CFT particulars within 10 working days; if the dispute-scheme membership certificate is deficient, enroll with an alternative approved scheme and reapply; if registration is declined, seek internal review by the FMA with fresh documentary evidence and apply to the District Court for judicial review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: AML/CFT Reporting Entity Registration and Compliance Programme Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Internal Affairs (DIA) — AML/CFT Group (Supervision and Enforcement), Wellington
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Effective before issuing virtual cards, register the IC as a reporting entity under section 130 of the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (AML/CFT Act). Submit the risk assessment covering the virtual-card payment rails (Mastercard/Visa), reload mechanisms, cardholder jurisdictions, merchant categories, and the TPP relationship; draw on the New Zealand National Risk Assessment. Adopt a board-approved AML/CFT Compliance Programme that meets ss 40-52, including CDD/EDD, ongoing monitoring, suspicious transaction reporting to the FIU, sanctions screening, record-keeping, and annual independent audit; appoint a NZ-based AML/CFT Compliance Officer; file the annual summary and assurance review with the DIA.
required_dossiers: AML/CFT reporting-entity registration form (DIA online)
ML/TF Risk Assessment document (IC-specific, payment rails and card markets)
AML/CFT Compliance Programme (board minutes of adoption)
AML/CFT Compliance Officer appointment resolution
Independent assurance/audit engagement letter (QSA or chartered accountant)
Policies on sanctions (UNSCR/Sanctions Act 2019), politically exposed persons, and enhanced due diligence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DIA issues an information request or risk-rating adjustment, respond within the prescribed 10 business days and amend the risk assessment using the DIA's sectoral guidance; if the programme is found materially deficient, commission a qualified AML consultant to redesign and obtain board ratification; where a risk-reduction notice is issued, comply with the conditions and submit a remediation implementation plan within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Card Scheme Membership, BIN Sponsorship and PCI DSS Level 1 Certification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Mastercard International Incorporated and Visa Worldwide Pte Limited (scheme rule enforcement); sponsor bank licensed by the Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Negotiate and execute a BIN Sponsorship and Programme Manager Agreement with one or more RBNZ-licensed New Zealand sponsor banks, under which the IC obtains a dedicated BIN range for Mastercard and/or Visa virtual-card issuance. Complete Mastercard's Registration of Principal and Visa's Third-Party Processor (TPP) enrolment dossiers, including network contact data, sub-processor lists, and programme scope. Achieve Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI DSS v4.0) compliance — perform a self-assessment questionnaire (SAQ-D) or an on-site Report on Compliance (ROC) through a Qualified Security Assessor — and deliver the Attestation of Compliance (AOC) to the sponsor. Submit the card product specification, spend-management controls, IP geolocation/travel restrictions, and transaction monitoring frameworks for scheme certification.
required_dossiers: Signed BIN Sponsorship Agreement with the NZ sponsor bank
Mastercard Principal Registration and Visa TPP Registration packages
PCI DSS v4.0 Attestation of Compliance (SAQ-D or QSA ROC)
Network security architecture diagrams and sub-processor listing
Card programme implementation plan (BIN range, card art, product config)
Sponsor bank's AML/CFT due-diligence questionnaire and corporate approval
Corporate guarantee or security trust if required by the sponsor
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a sponsor bank declines the BIN sponsorship, approach three alternative RBNZ-licensed sponsors with an enhanced remediation plan and conduct PCI gap testing via a QSA; if the card scheme rejects the programme, correct the compliance gap, resubmit the TPP/Principal application and facilitate scheme audit; in a serious delay scenario, use a licensed white-label BIN issuer until direct sponsorship is granted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Formation Governance Ratification — First Board Meeting and Officer Appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors and the New Zealand registered office (statutory record-keeping function)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first full board meeting (or execute circular written resolutions under s 107 of the Companies Act 1993) at the registered office. Approve and ratify all acts and costs of the incorporators and attorneys completed at the formation stage; ratify the subscriber share allotments; adopt the governance charter and delegation registers; confirm appointment of the Managing Director, CFO, Company Secretary, and AML/CFT Compliance Officer; approve banking/joint-signing mandates and the virtual-card treasury account architecture; pass the initial accounting policy, balance-date determination, and auditor engagement if relevant. Issue share certificates bearing the seal or electronic equivalent.
required_dossiers: Agenda and notice of first board meeting (or waiver of notice)
Minutes of first board meeting or circular written resolutions
Share register and share certificates
Directors' interests register (ss 140-145, Companies Act 1993)
Bank signing authority mandate and card-program governance resolution
Corporate Governance Charter and committee charters
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any pre-incorporation act is outside the directors' authority, ratify the act under the Companies Act 1993 agency provisions and record the ratification in an ex post facto board resolution; if a shareholder challenges the officer appointment, convene an extraordinary general meeting within 30 days; if minutes are deficient, re-execute the resolution with full deliberation and preserve statutory records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Annual Corporate Compliance, Registry Post-Incorporation Filings, Levies and Ongoing Obligations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Inland Revenue, Department of Internal Affairs (AML/CFT), FSP Registrar and FMA (sector levies)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Maintain the IC's good standing by filing the Companies Office annual return (Form AR) within 40 working days after the balance date, and remitting the Companies Office levy and FMA financial services levy per the current fee schedules. File all IRD returns (GST if registered, NRWT quarterly, RWT, and annual tax return) electronically; file the DIA AML/CFT annual summary and independent auditor's assurance report; confirm and renew FSP registration data and dispute resolution scheme membership annually; if the IC is a small ordinary company, either prepare XRB A1 financial statements or pass an opt-out resolution for shareholders' notification. The directors must maintain a ROC/risk register and update the Companies Register on any change of directors, shareholders, registered office, or constitution.
required_dossiers: Form AR (Annual Return) filed with the Companies Office
Companies Office levy and FMA financial sector levy payment receipts
IRD GST, NRWT, RWT and corporate tax returns
AML/CFT annual summary report and independent assurance review
FSP Register annual confirmation and dispute resolution scheme membership renewal
Board-approved XRB A1 financial statements or shareholder opt-out notice
Updated directors' and shareholders' registers in the Companies Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an annual return is late, file promptly and apply for late-filing penalty relief; if the company has been removed or struck off, applicant must apply under s 386 or s 387 of the Companies Act 1993 for restoration, paying all outstanding levies; if the AML/CFT report is missed, submit within 30 days with an explanation and amended supervisory statement, avoiding enforcement action by the DIA; for FSP registration lapses, file reinstatement and corrective disclosures to the FSP Registrar.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: New Zealand Companies Office — Registrar of Financial Service Providers (MBIE) for FSP licensing; Department of Internal Affairs (AML/CFT Group) for AML/CFT registration; Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) via licensed sponsor banks for card-scheme prudential oversight; Mastercard and Visa for payment network scheme authorization
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Financial Service Provider (FSP) Registration — category for 'issuing and managing means of payment' (virtual expense cards) and 'money or value transfer services' under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008; AML/CFT reporting entity registration under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009; card-network BIN Sponsorship and Programme Manager approval through an RBNZ-licensed sponsoring bank

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) New Zealand, acting under the Resource Management Act 1991 and the Environmental Protection Authority Act 2011
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration tier only — no full Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) or resource consent is required for the IC's virtual-card issuing, back-office accounting, and software-development operations because the activity is wholly commercial, office-based, and does not fall within Schedule 4 of the Resource Management Act 1991 as an environmentally significant industry; a low-impact activity notice may be recorded with the territorial authority where a physical card personalization or light warehouse facility is used
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOC, NOx, or PM10 point-source emissions are anticipated. Any physical office/dispatch facility must comply with (i) the NZ Building Code Water Supplies and Sanitary Drainage provisions (Clauses G4 and W4), (ii) the local council Trade Waste Bylaw for office sanitary discharge, and (iii) the National Environmental Standards for Air Quality 2004, including particulate matter (PM10) annual mean not exceeding 50 μg/m³, NO2 annual mean not exceeding 100 μg/m³, and CO not exceeding 10 mg/m³; data-centre and server-room cooling must use closed-loop refrigerants with zero ozone-depletion potential and no chlorofluorocarbon emissions; any standby diesel generator requires a permitted-activity resource consent governed by the National Environmental Standards for Air Quality (diesel generator emission limit for PM10 of 0.5 g/kWh).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Building Warrant of Fitness (BWoF) and annual fire-safety systems certificate issued under ss 102-111 of the Building Act 2004 and Clauses C1-C6 of the NZ Building Code, including fire alarms, emergency lighting, sprinklers/egress paths, and a completed Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) evacuation scheme where the premises contain more than 10 workers; structural load inspection and floor-loading certification for the card-personalization vault or server racks; Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 (HSWA) workplace risk assessment, first-aid, hazard register, and incident-report protocol; AS/NZS 3000 electrical wiring compliance and periodic electrical safety inspection issued by a licensed electrician; Civil Defence Emergency Management Act 2002 continuity planning, including backup-power battery systems, earthquake-strap of server racks, and personnel shelter arrangements.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Te Tari Taake) of New Zealand; online portal: myIR at https://ird.govt.nz.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-incorporated International Company that is not a New Zealand resident must first register with the New Zealand Companies Office as an overseas company (or incorporate locally) and then apply for a New Zealand IRD number on Form IR596 (Company IRD Number Application) via the myIR portal or by post to Inland Revenue, attaching the certificate of incorporation, constitutional documents, directors' details, and evidence of a New Zealand address for service. The IRD number is issued within 8-10 business days. The same registration form contains a check-box for GST registration, which simultaneously activates the GST account where a taxable activity exists or is intended.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone (Territorial application: non-resident International Company is taxable in New Zealand only on New Zealand-source income under sections YD 1-YD 4 of the Income Tax Act 2007; offshore virtual-card issuing, interchange, and treasury income is outside the New Zealand tax net, and no New Zealand sub-national income tax is imposed).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not operate a check-the-box or deemed-classification system. The income tax treatment is statutory rather than elective. A non-resident International Company is taxed at the corporate rate of 28%, except that effective 'tax-exempt zone' outcomes for offshore income arise automatically under the territorial rules. Election mechanisms available under New Zealand law include: voluntary GST registration under section 51 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985; GST grouping election under section 55; GST branch registration election under section 54; and the former 'qualifying company' election and look-through company (LTC) election under Subpart HB of the Income Tax Act 2007, but LTC status is generally unavailable to a non-resident International Company with non-resident shareholders. Hybrid mismatch rules under Subpart FH (OECD BEPS Action 2) operate automatically and disallow tax advantages from hybrid financial dealings.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies made in New Zealand (including zero-rated exported services but excluding exempt financial services) in the current or immediately preceding 12-month period. Compulsory registration applies to any non-resident supplier once this threshold is exceeded; voluntary registration is available from the first dollar, with refund entitlement conditioned upon registration being compulsory or the supplier conducting an exporting business.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, no pre-clearance API, and no digital stamping regime is imposed by the Inland Revenue Department. e-Invoicing is voluntary and operates on the PEPPOL network under the New Zealand e-Invoicing programme. GST invoices must include the supplier's name, IRD/GST number, NZBN, invoice date, description and quantity of supply, consideration and tax included; invoices must be issued within 28 days of the end of the taxable period. GST returns are filed electronically through myIR on monthly, two-monthly, or six-monthly cycles. Transactions are not subject to government fiscal API clearance; however, Mastercard and Visa commercial interchange reporting is contractually mandatory for the card-issuing fintech but does not constitute a tax-clearance mechanism.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: zero-rated under sections 11(1)(a)-(e) of the GST Act where goods are physically exported to a destination outside New Zealand within 28 days of supply, supplied as stores for international aircraft or ships, or supplied to a non-resident who is outside New Zealand at the time of supply and the goods are subsequently exported. Services: zero-rated under section 11A of the GST Act where (a) the services are supplied to a non-resident recipient who is outside New Zealand at the time of supply and the services are not supplied under an arrangement with a New Zealand-resident person, or (b) the services are performed directly in connection with goods exported by the supplier, or (c) the services are financial services supplied to a non-resident recipient who is outside New Zealand when the services are performed. For the corporate virtual-card issuer, card issuing, transaction processing, interchange, spend-control, and settlement services supplied to non-resident corporate clients (merchants or cardholders) qualify as zero-rated exported financial services provided the recipient is not in New Zealand at the time of supply and the services do not relate to New Zealand land, goods, or a New Zealand resident. Services supplied to New Zealand-resident cardholders or merchants are exempt financial services under section 14(1)(a) of the GST Act, which are neither taxable nor zero-rated and therefore do not create input tax recovery rights.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: New Zealand Customs Service Export Entry (electronic declaration via Trade Single Window / Class ImpEx) for physical goods movements
Bill of Lading / House Air Waybill / Master Air Waybill evidencing export from New Zealand within 28 days of supply
Inward Foreign Currency Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 from a registered bank proving payment for the exported supply
Signed service agreement or card programme agreement identifying the non-resident customer's jurisdiction and confirming place of consumption
Non-residence evidence for each recipient (foreign certificate of incorporation, tax residence certificate, or foreign registry extract)
GST invoice issued in accordance with section 24 of the GST Act, explicitly stating 'zero-rated' and citing section 11A for exported services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Inland Revenue Department heavily audits zero-rating claims under the Tax Administration Act 1994 (TAA) and the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985. If zero-rating is improperly claimed, the supply is treated as standard-rated; the IRD will reassess the full 15% GST with retrospective clawback for the entire audit period, plus use-of-money interest (currently 9.33% per annum). Shortfall penalties under section 141 of the TAA escalate from 20% for lack of reasonable care to 40% for gross carelessness, 100% for knowingly obtaining an incorrect tax advantage, and 150% for evasion. Criminal prosecution may be initiated under sections 143A and 143B of the TAA with fines up to NZD 50,000 per offence and imprisonment for up to 5 years for tax evasion or knowingly providing false GST returns. False customs export declarations are separately sanctionable under the Customs and Excise Act 2018, with penalties up to NZD 10,000 per declaration, plus potential deregistration from the approved exporter scheme and publication of the adverse assessment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua), as the central banking authority for registered banks, settlement systems, and foreign exchange clearing infrastructure; the Financial Markets Authority and Department of Internal Affairs serve as co-regulators for AML/CFT supervision of non-bank financial institutions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand operates a freely convertible currency regime under Article VIII of the IMF Articles of Agreement. There are no exchange control laws requiring central bank approval for current account or capital account transactions. Profit remittances, dividends, interest, and capital repatriations are permitted without quantitative restriction, subject only to withholding taxes (RWT/NRWT), the Overseas Investment Act 2023 consent thresholds in cases involving sensitive land or significant business assets, and standard bank anti-money-laundering due diligence. The New Zealand dollar (NZD) is fully fungible across domestic and offshore liquidity pools, and there are no surrender, rationing, or multiple-tier exchange rate mechanisms.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: New Zealand has no statutory export proceeds surrender requirement or mandatory conversion ratio. Exporters may retain foreign currency earnings in New Zealand or offshore accounts without obligation to convert into NZD. Inward and outward remittances are subject to monetary reporting thresholds for balance of payments statistical purposes only, and settlement banks generally require a narrative purpose code and supporting commercial documents for large transactions.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Australia and New Zealand Banking Group (New Zealand) Limited (ANZ Bank New Zealand Ltd)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Conditional / Restricted. Offshore electronic money institutions (EMIs) are not eligible for a New Zealand registered bank license without incorporating a local prudentially regulated entity. An offshore EMI may operate as a non-bank payment service provider only through a locally incorporated New Zealand company registered under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008 and enrolled in an approved dispute resolution scheme, while also satisfying the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (AML/CFT Act). However, major New Zealand banks generally classify offshore EMIs as high-risk financial institution counterparties and will either decline account opening or require a physical New Zealand office, local independent directors, comprehensive compliance audit statements, and a formal settlement account arrangement with a licensed sponsor bank. End-to-end account opening through a pure digital EMI without local substance is unlikely to succeed.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For non-resident corporate and high-risk business types such as a virtual card issuer, New Zealand banks are not statutorily required to mandate an in-person board appearance, but most mainstream registered banks will require either (a) physical attendance of at least one director or authorized signatory at a New Zealand branch, or (b) a secure audio-visual KYC interview supplemented by notarized corporate documents and live verification of original identification. At least one local director or nominated agent with New Zealand connection is frequently required for company authorization, and the bank must identify all ultimate beneficial owners with minimum 25% economic interest. Pure remote account opening without any physical or locally represented party is generally unavailable for this industry niche until a full compliance relationship is established.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The company is an International Company (IC) with tax-exempt-zone classification, which may present as a shell or tax avoidance structure to New Zealand compliance departments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide authenticated Certificate of Incorporation and Constitution from the New Zealand Companies Office; current certificate of registration / annual return; the IC's deferred tax-exempt status certificate or legal opinion from a New Zealand tax counsel explaining the tax classification; proof of economic substance including employment of New Zealand or nonresident advisers, contractual agreements, operational expenses, and a board resolution detailing a genuine treasury and card-issuing business purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Virtual card issuance (ISIC 6619 / NAICS 522320) is treated as a high-risk, high-volume financial activity with potential for stored value, money movement, and insufficient transaction traceability.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bankable business plan demonstrating licensed program management through Mastercard/Visa; fully executed BIN sponsor or program manager agreement; detailed transaction flow diagrams for virtual card issuance, settlement, and chargeback handling; policies and procedures for customer due diligence, ongoing transaction monitoring, suspicious activity reporting, sanctions screening, and cardholder verification; evidence of appointment of a New Zealand AML/CFT compliance officer and internal auditor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership obscured by discretionary trust structures, offshore directors, or multiple layered corporate entities.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: An updated Ultimate Beneficial Ownership (UBO) Schedule at the 25% threshold with passport copies; trust deed, trustee appointment, and current trust resolution identifying settlors, trustees, and any additional class of beneficiaries; organization chart of all legal entities with shareholdings; explanation of source of funds and source of wealth for each UBO; official background check and regulatory clearance certificates from the country of residence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Negative press, sanctions exposure, or association with high-risk FATF/AML jurisdictions in the card payment ecosystem.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions and adverse-media screening report from professional screening tools for all directors, UBOs, and the entire corporate tree; detailed jurisdictional risk matrix showing low-risk geographies of cardholders and merchants; proposed restrictive list for prohibited countries; contractual commitment to comply with New Zealand sanctions legislation and produce periodic certification to the bank's compliance team.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection or operational cash flows are inconsistent with the revenue model and may trigger suspicion of disguised money laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited or reviewed financial statements for the prior period; management accounts showing expected issuance volumes, interchange, and merchant pricing; bank statements for any existing banking platforms; procurement agreements with technology vendors and network processors; invoice and payment forecast model; board-approved treasury policy and inflation-adjusted capital adequacy projections.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections into the New Zealand International Company should be routed through the settlement bank using SWIFT MT103 with the following protocol: (i) remitter field must reference the shareholder name and country of source; (ii) field 70 (Remittance Information) must include the capital purpose code `Supplemental Capital Contribution` and the unique board resolution reference; (iii) field 72 may include authorized signature identifiers; (iv) for USD/EUR allocations, use the bank's correspondent account and confirm the final beneficiary is the regression-validated New Zealand entity account. Supporting documentation must be pre-delivered to the receiving bank: updated Certificate of Incorporation, board resolution approving the capital raise, shareholder subscription agreement, investor source-of-funds declaration, and any Overseas Investment Act 2023 clearance letter if the injection crosses thresholds applicable to non-resident acquisitions. As New Zealand does not maintain exchange control approval, banks routinely process such payments in original currency without buy/sell restriction; however, the bank may impose a temporary hold until UBO verification and purpose-code validation are completed.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements are executed through (a) direct cross-border payments via SWIFT MT103 for supplier payments, license fees, and intercompany settlements; (b) commercial letters of credit opened through the sponsoring bank's trade finance platform, using MT700 for issuance and MT760 for guarantee issuance; (c) NZD-denominated domestic payments through the bank's clearing product using the New Zealand Clearing House System (AONZ), with same-day or next-day settlement depending on the clearing batch; and (d) high-value settlements through the Reserve Bank's Exchange Settlement Account System (ESAS) via real-time gross settlement. For virtual card issuer treasury flows, settlement files are accrued in the card scheme's internal settlement ledger and net-settled on T+1 using SWIFT paid-or-received messages, with the final funding leg in NZD via domestic SWIFT or in USD/EUR via the bank's correspondent network. The bank should be notified of the anticipated settlement schedule and permitted to review the scheme rules for mandatory funding buffers.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable spot and outright forward contracts (FXA) in NZD/USD, NZD/EUR, NZD/GBP, and AUD/NZD for core treasury exposures

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in restricted or non-clearing currency pairs, such as CNH, KRW, INR, and TWD, where required to hedge non-convertible counterparty exposures through a licensed New Zealand dealer
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for minimizing interest and principal cash flow mismatch in borrowing structures
European-style FX options and outright option combinations for downside protection on projected virtual card settlement volumes
Foreign currency swap and rolling swap arrangements executed under a valid ISDA and New Zealand Financial Markets Conduct Act exemption or dealer licensing arrangement

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one calendar month after each anniversary of incorporation (the annual return date)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZD 161.50 applies; continued non-compliance triggers a Notice of Intention to Remove and strike-off from the Companies Register, along with potential director fines up to NZD 10,000.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Markets Authority (FMA) through the Financial Service Providers Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one calendar month after each annual confirmation date (anniversary of FSP registration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to confirm results in removal from the FSP Register, loss of eligibility to provide financial services in New Zealand, and civil penalties of up to NZD 100,000.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Markets Authority (FMA) or other designated AML/CFT supervisor
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the entity's balance date (or as directed by the supervisor)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Supervisory compliance order, civil penalties up to NZD 2 million, and potential suspension or revocation of the AML/CFT registration or approval.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit applies to any FMC reporting entity classified as 'large', i.e., meeting at least two of three criteria in consecutive periods: total assets exceeding NZD 30 million, total revenue exceeding NZD 30 million, and 50 or more full-time equivalent employees; licensed financial service providers may also be subject to audit as a condition of the Financial Markets Conduct licence.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand Equivalents to IFRS (NZ IFRS) for for-profit entities, or New Zealand Generally Accepted Accounting Practice (NZ GAAP) for smaller reporting entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The annual return must disclose current shareholders and shareholdings as at the annual return date; all share transfers must be recorded in the Register of Members before filing. For AML/CFT purposes, beneficial ownership is refreshed at least annually and any identified change of control is updated in the company's internal beneficial ownership records within 20 working days.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 28% (standard New Zealand corporate tax rate for resident companies under Part A of Schedule 1, Income Tax Act 2007)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays exist in New Zealand. The effective rate may be reduced by the 15% R&D Tax Incentive (RDTI), the 20% growth R&D credit, and the imputation credit system. A Cook Islands 'International Company' that is non-resident is not taxed on foreign-sourced income; only New Zealand-sourced business profits are taxed at 28% (if attributed to a fixed establishment) or by final non-resident withholding tax for passive income.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite (no statutory expiry; subject to greater-than-49% continuity of ownership or the same-business test)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 (Company Income Tax Return) filed electronically through Inland Revenue's myIR portal; non-resident companies with New Zealand-source income may file IR4NS (Non-Resident Company Return).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; three provisional tax instalments are made during the year (for standard 31 March balance date: 28 August, 15 January, 7 May).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For the standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 is due on 7 July (or 31 March of the following year if a tax agent holds an extension of time). For non-standard balance dates, the return is due by the 7th day of the second month following the balance date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate assessable income from all sources, including card issuance fees, interchange-related fees, spend-management fees, and interest earned on customer float.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only New Zealand-sourced income attributed to business carried on through a fixed establishment in New Zealand. Foreign-sourced income is outside the New Zealand tax net for a non-resident International Company.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Interest, Dividends and Other Investment Income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report dividends, interest, royalties and other passive income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include New Zealand-sourced passive income subject to non-resident withholding tax. Foreign-source passive income is excluded unless the company is treaty-resident in New Zealand.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Expenses incurred in deriving assessable income; e.g., card network costs, software, personnel, AML compliance, bank charges, and professional fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only expenses specifically incurred in deriving New Zealand-sourced income; apportion overseas head-office overheads on a commercially defensible basis and maintain records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add back capital expenditure, penalties, entertainment expense, and other statutorily non-deductible amounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Same treatment; penalty payments, including AML/CFT penalties and NRWT surcharges, cannot be deducted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Carry forward and offset prior-year tax losses to current year income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident may only use losses attributable to New Zealand-source business activity, subject to the continuity of ownership and same-business tests.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Assessed income or loss after all additions and offsets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the company has no fixed establishment in New Zealand, the assessable result should reflect only NZ-source passive income; business profits may be nil.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 - Tax on Net Taxable Income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute 28% company tax on the net taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For payers of passive income, the amount of tax is the NRWT or treaty-reduced withholding calculated on the gross amount, not the net profit-based IR4 calculation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 - Tax Credits (RWT, Provisional, Foreign Tax)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim resident withholding tax, provisional tax instalments, approved issuer levy, and foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only New Zealand tax credits apply. A non-resident cannot claim foreign tax credits against NZ-source withholding tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 9 - Refund or Terminal Tax Due
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The net amount of tax payable or refundable after credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any over-withheld NRWT/treaty tax may be claimed through an IRD refund application.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of NZ$250 for a company return; late payment penalty of 4% of unpaid tax at the due date, then 1% per month (or part-month) thereafter; use-of-money interest (UOMI) is charged at 8.38% per annum (2024-25 rates) on underpaid provisional and terminal tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) on dividends is 30% (or 15% for fully imputed dividends paid to non-residents). DTA reductions apply.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the non-resident recipient must obtain a Certificate of Residence (TRC) from its jurisdiction of residence, deliver it to the New Zealand payer prior to payment, and complete the IRD's rate-reduction notification. The payer withholds at the reduced DTA rate; if excess NRWT was deducted, the non-resident may claim a refund from Inland Revenue by filing a non-resident income tax return within the statutory period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory NRWT on interest to non-residents is 15%; this can be reduced to 2% Approved Issuer Levy (AIL) if the New Zealand borrower is an approved issuer and the interest is paid to a non-associated non-resident. Statutory royalties NRWT is 15%; DTA reductions may lower interest/royalties to 0-10% depending on the treaty.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: New Zealand legislation does not prescribe a fixed NZD de minimis; contemporaneous documentation is expected for all attributable cross-border controlled transactions. Mandatory Master File/Local File and Country-by-Country Report thresholds apply to multinational groups with global consolidated turnover exceeding NZ$130 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not have domestic Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) analogous to offshore centres. Instead, the general anti-avoidance rule (GAAR) and source rules require a genuine New Zealand fixed establishment for non-resident business profits, and the AML/CFT Act 2009 mandates substantive presence, NZ-based officers, and on-site compliance systems for payment services.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly omitting or mischaracterising income in the IR4, creating fictitious invoices or card 'interchange' payments to connected shell entities, or hiding New Zealand-source profits in tax-exempt International Company accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil shortfall penalty up to 300% of the tax shortfall (Tax Administration Act 1994, ss 141E-K); criminal liability under s 143A for evasion with imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to NZ$150,000; unpaid tax, interest and UOMI remain recoverable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly participate are jointly and severally liable for the shortfall and may face civil restitution, asset restraint orders, court-imposed travel bans during criminal proceedings, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing an International Company with no employees, premises or independent control, used as a conduit to route card fees and 'royalties' from New Zealand customers to a tax-haven parent without arm's-length pricing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Commissioner can reconstruct the arrangement under the GAAR (s BG1) and apply transfer pricing adjustments. An 'abusive tax position' triggers a 100% shortfall penalty, and failure to provide documents may produce a 20% administratively imposed penalty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false transfer-pricing documentation are exposed to director penalties under the Tax Administration Act, may be disqualified under the Companies Act 1993, and can be the subject of civil recovery proceedings; travel restrictions may be imposed pending tax debt investigations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing corporate virtual cards without registration as an AML/CFT reporting entity and without holding the required financial service provider licence; failing to perform customer due diligence, source-of-funds checks, or reporting suspicious transactions arising from card-funded fraud or tax evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the AML/CFT Act 2009, a body corporate faces civil penalties up to NZ$2 million per breach, and individuals up to NZ$200,000; criminal liability for money laundering carries up to 7 years' imprisonment and fines up to NZ$300,000. De-registration from the FSP register and public enforcement notices also apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and senior officers may be personally prosecuted for knowingly facilitating money laundering, receive civil fines, be made subject to asset forfeiture and restitution orders, be forbidden from leaving New Zealand pending trial, and be disqualified from managing companies.
